description: Costco noise patterns for production-safe parser classification

classification_policy.description: noise classification must be applied only after item_detail, discount_detail, subtotal, and total checks fail

header_patterns.description: receipt header or column guide lines

internal_code_patterns.description: internal tracking / system code lines that are not item or discount data

safe_guard_rules.name: protect_item_detail_lines
safe_guard_rules.rule: If line matches any item_detail pattern, do not classify as noise

safe_guard_rules.name: protect_discount_detail_lines
safe_guard_rules.rule: If line matches any discount_detail pattern, do not classify as noise

safe_guard_rules.name: protect_summary_lines
safe_guard_rules.rule: If line matches subtotal or total pattern, do not classify as noise
safe_guard_rules.description: summary lines must be handled by summary_patterns.json

safe_guard_rules.name: protect_price_like_lines
safe_guard_rules.rule: If line contains a valid price-like numeric structure and also matches store item/discount patterns, do not classify as noise

fallback_policy.description: Only assign noise after all item, discount, and summary classifications fail

output_policy.description: noise lines should remain in parser output for traceability and debugging

parser_notes: Do not classify a line as noise before checking item_detail, discount_detail, subtotal, and total patterns.
Do not use broad uppercase-prefix regex such as ^\*[A-Z]+ because it can over-match valid transactional lines.
Do not use heuristic rules like 'non-numeric text means noise' because valid item_name lines can be text-only.
Header fragments may appear split across lines; parser should handle merged-header logic separately.
semantic_notes: noise lines are not active semantic targets
noise lines should still be handed off for traceability and context preservation
